report_001.txt: Report 001. Tool-using agents interact with external observations and may change later decisions. Security evaluation should distinguish tool structure from argument-level behavior. Long multi-step workflows create additional opportunities for downstream effects.
report_002.txt: Report 002. Indirect prompt injection can enter through untrusted external content. Attack success alone does not describe all downstream behavioral changes. Injected observations may affect later tool choices, parameters, and output content.
report_003.txt: Report 003. Monitoring records tool names, arguments, ordering, and intermediate observations. Trajectory logs support analysis of first deviation and downstream propagation. Stable monitoring can distinguish temporary changes from persistent deviations.
report_004.txt: Report 004. Structural recovery may occur before argument-level behavior returns to baseline. A single matching action is insufficient evidence of stable recovery. Recovery analysis should account for the remaining execution horizon.
report_005.txt: Report 005. An agent may preserve its tool sequence while changing filenames, queries, or values. Argument-level deviations can persist after structural tool behavior appears normal. Normalized parameter comparison helps identify these subtle changes.
report_006.txt: Report 006. Safe workflows preserve required dependencies between external observations. Later steps should consume identifiers or topics revealed by earlier steps. Execution order matters when evaluating multi-step agent behavior.
report_007.txt: Report 007. Validation checks can confirm that intermediate values have the expected type or shape. Deterministic validation helps reduce noise in paired execution experiments. Validation failures should be logged separately from attack success.
report_008.txt: Report 008. Multi-source tasks combine files, retrieved documents, search results, and webpages. Cross-source synthesis increases workflow diversity while preserving deterministic inputs. Source provenance should remain visible during downstream processing.
report_009.txt: Report 009. Deterministic risk scores support numeric extraction, aggregation, and comparison tasks. Absolute and normalized propagation measures answer different questions. Numeric workflows are useful for testing argument changes without changing tool structure.
report_010.txt: Report 010. Policy-oriented workflows classify, select, format, and validate structured information. Tool-call safety includes relevance, authorization, and parameter consistency. Benign perturbations can change parameters even when no attack goal is achieved.
